questions.stem: Look at this series: 9, 16, 23, 30, 37, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: Each term is seven more than the one before, so 37 + 7 = 44. You get 43 by reading the step as six, 45 by reading it as eight and 51 by adding seven twice.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 98, 85, 72, 59, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: The series drops by 13 each time, so 59 - 13 = 46. You get 72 by adding the step instead of subtracting it, 47 by using a step of 12 and 33 by subtracting 13 twice.

questions.stem: Look at this series: ___, 68, 60, 52, 44. What number should come first?
questions.explanation: The series falls by eight, so the term before 68 is 68 + 8 = 76. You get 84 by stepping back twice, 74 by using a step of six and 60 by moving forward through the series instead of backward.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 18, 25, 32, ___, 46, 53. What number is missing?
questions.explanation: The step is seven throughout, so the missing term is 32 + 7 = 39, which also checks against 46 - 7. You get 40 from a step of eight, 38 from a step of six and 45 by counting back only one from 46.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 85, 74, 63, 52, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: Each term is 11 less than the one before, so 52 - 11 = 41. You get 63 by adding 11 instead of subtracting, 42 by using a step of ten and 30 by subtracting 11 twice.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 7, 16, 25, 34, ___, ___ What two numbers should come next?
questions.explanation: The series adds nine each time, so the next two terms are 43 and 52. The pairs starting at 42 come from a step of eight and 52 and 61 come from starting one step too far along.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 5, 7, 11, 17, 25, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: The gaps grow by two: 2, 4, 6, 8, so the next gap is ten and 25 + 10 = 35. You get 33 by repeating the last gap of eight, 37 by jumping the gap to 12 and 47 by taking two more steps instead of one.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 2, 4, ___, 256. What number is missing?
questions.explanation: Each term is the square of the one before it: 2 x 2 = 4, 4 x 4 = 16 and 16 x 16 = 256, so the missing term is 16. You get eight by taking the first step, doubling, as the rule for every step, which would end the series at 16 rather than 256. You get 12 by assuming the multiplier climbs by one, two then three. You get 128 by working backwards from 256 and halving it, which assumes the last step is a doubling.

questions.stem: Look at this series: ___, 6, 9, 14, 21, 30. What number should come first?
questions.explanation: The gaps are 3, 5, 7 and 9, so the gap before 6 is one and the first term is 5. You get 3 by using the next gap up, 4 by using a gap of two and 1 by using a gap of five.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 4, 9, 17, ___, 42, 59. What number is missing?
questions.explanation: The gaps grow by three: 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, so the missing term is 17 + 11 = 28, which checks against 42 - 14. You get 25 by assuming a constant gap of eight, 29 by using a gap of 12 and 31 by counting back 11 from 42 instead of 14.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 3, 4, 7, 12, 19, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: The gaps are the odd numbers 1, 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is nine and 19 + 9 = 28. You get 26 by repeating the gap of seven, 30 by jumping to 11 and 39 by taking two more steps.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 90, 87, 81, 72, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: The series falls by 3, then 6, then 9, so the next drop is 12 and 72 - 12 = 60. You get 63 by holding the step at nine, 57 by jumping to 15 and 45 by taking two more steps.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 2, 6, 18, 54, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: Each term is three times the one before, so 54 x 3 = 162. You get 108 by doubling, 216 by multiplying by four and 486 by multiplying by three twice.

questions.stem: Look at this series: ___, 15, 75, 375. What number should come first?
questions.explanation: Each term is five times the one before, so the first term is 15 divided by five, which is 3. You get 5 by dividing by three, 10 by subtracting five and 75 by multiplying instead of dividing.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 486, 162, 54, 18, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: Each term is the one before divided by three, so 18 divided by three is 6. You get 9 by halving, 3 by dividing by three twice and 2 by dividing by nine.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 4, 10, 28, 82, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: The rule is multiply by three, then subtract two, so 82 x 3 - 2 = 244. You get 246 by forgetting the subtraction, 240 by subtracting two before multiplying and 730 by running the rule twice.

questions.stem: Look at this series: ___, 10, 24, 52, 108. What number should come first?
questions.explanation: The rule is double, then add four, so working backward from 10 you subtract four and then halve: (10 - 4) divided by two is 3. You get 6 by subtracting four without halving, 5 by halving without subtracting and 1 by halving before subtracting.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 4, 20, 7, 25, 10, 30, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: Two series take turns: 4, 7, 10 adds three and 20, 25, 30 adds five, and it is the first series' turn, so the answer is 13. You get 35 by continuing only the second series, 33 by adding three to 30 and 15 by adding five to 10.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 3, 4, 8, 17, 33, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: The gaps are the square numbers in order: 4 - 3 = 1, 8 - 4 = 4, 17 - 8 = 9 and 33 - 17 = 16, so the next gap is 25 and 33 + 25 = 58. You get 49 by holding the gap at 16 instead of moving on to the next square. You get 56 by treating the gaps as an ordinary growing sequence: they rise by three, then five, then seven, so keeping that rise at seven gives a gap of 23. You get 65 by assuming the gap doubles, from 16 to 32.

questions.stem: Look at this series: ___, 9, 5, 18, 8, 36, 11. What number should come first?
questions.explanation: The odd positions hold one series (___, 5, 8, 11, adding three) and the even positions hold another (9, 18, 36, doubling), so the first term is 5 - 3 = 2. You get 8 by adding three instead of subtracting, 3 by subtracting two and 1 by subtracting four.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 1, 6, 4, 11, 9, 16, 16, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: One series runs 1, 4, 9, 16 and the other runs 6, 11, 16 adding five, and the next turn belongs to the second one, so the answer is 21. You get 25 or 36 by continuing the first series instead and 22 by adding six rather than five.

questions.stem: Look at this series: \(\frac{1}{2}\), \(\frac{3}{4}\), \(\frac{9}{8}\), \(\frac{27}{16}\), ... What term should come next?
questions.explanation: Each term multiplies the one before by \(\frac{3}{2}\), so the numerator triples and the denominator doubles. Tripling the numerator only gives \(\frac{81}{16}\), doubling the denominator only gives \(\frac{27}{32}\) and tripling both gives \(\frac{81}{48}\).

questions.stem: Look at this series: \(\frac{1}{6}\), \(\frac{1}{3}\), \(\frac{1}{2}\), \(\frac{2}{3}\), ... What term should come next?
questions.explanation: Written over sixths the series reads \(\frac{1}{6}\), \(\frac{2}{6}\), \(\frac{3}{6}\), \(\frac{4}{6}\), so it adds \(\frac{1}{6}\) and the next term is \(\frac{5}{6}\). You get \(\frac{1}{3}\) by adding the numerators and denominators straight across, \(\frac{3}{4}\) by adding only \(\frac{1}{12}\) and \(1\) by adding \(\frac{1}{3}\).

questions.stem: Look at this series: ___, \(\frac{7}{10}\), \(\frac{7}{15}\), \(\frac{7}{20}\), \(\frac{7}{25}\). What term should come first?
questions.explanation: The numerator stays 7 and the denominator climbs by five, so the denominator before ten is five and the first term is \(\frac{7}{5}\). You get \(\frac{7}{30}\) by running the series forward instead of backward, \(\frac{7}{6}\) by stepping the denominator back only four and \(\frac{1}{5}\) by taking five off the numerator instead.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 3.5, 0.4, 4.0, 0.9, 4.5, 1.4, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: Two series take turns and both add 0.5: 3.5, 4.0, 4.5 and 0.4, 0.9, 1.4. It is the first series' turn, so the answer is 5.0. You get 1.9 by continuing the second series, 4.6 by adding 0.1 and 5.5 by adding 0.5 twice.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 9.4, 8.7, 8.0, 7.3, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: The series drops by 0.7 each time, so 7.3 - 0.7 = 6.6. You get 6.5 from a step of 0.8, 5.9 by subtracting 0.7 twice and 6.0 by using 1.3, the gap between terms two places apart.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 0.4, 1.2, ___, 10.8, 32.4. What number is missing?
questions.explanation: Each term is three times the one before, so the missing term is 1.2 x 3 = 3.6, which checks against 10.8 divided by three. You get 2.4 by doubling, 4.8 by multiplying by four and 5.4 by dividing 10.8 by two.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 1.5, 2.25, 3.0, 3.75, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: The series adds 0.75 each time, so 3.75 + 0.75 = 4.5. You get 4.25 from a step of 0.5, 4.75 from a step of one and 5.25 by adding 0.75 twice.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 5, 40, 10, 35, 15, 30, ___, ___ What two numbers should come next?
questions.explanation: One series climbs by five (5, 10, 15, 20) and the other falls by five (40, 35, 30, 25), and the climbing one goes first, so the answer is 20 and 25. Reversing the two series gives 25 and 20, adding to the falling series gives 20 and 35 and continuing only the second series gives 35 and 40.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 2, 3, 6, 11, 18, ___, ___ What two numbers should come next?
questions.explanation: The gaps are the odd numbers 1, 3, 5, 7, so the next gaps are nine and 11, giving 27 and 38. You get 25 and 32 by holding the gap at seven, 27 and 36 by repeating the gap of nine and 29 and 42 by starting the gaps at 11.

questions.stem: Look at this series: BMC, DME, FMG, ___, JMK. What term is missing?
questions.explanation: The middle letter stays M while the outer letters each move ahead two, so after FMG comes HMI, which lines up with JMK. IMH has the right letters in the wrong order, HMJ pushes the last letter one too far and IMJ moves each outer letter three.

questions.stem: Look at this series: PDQ, PGT, PJW, ... What term should come next?
questions.explanation: P is held constant and the other two letters each advance three, so D, G, J becomes M and Q, T, W becomes Z. PMY moves the last letter only two, PLZ moves the middle letter only two and ZMP is the right letters reversed.

questions.stem: Look at this series: GT, HS, IR, JQ, ... What term should come next?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves forward one and the second moves backward one, so J becomes K and Q becomes P. KQ leaves the second letter alone, LP moves the first letter two and PK is the answer written backward.

questions.stem: Look at this series: ___, NW, OV, PU, QT. What term should come first?
questions.explanation: Reading backward, the first letter drops one and the second climbs one, so N becomes M and W becomes X. LX moves the first letter back two, MW leaves the second letter unchanged and XM is the answer reversed.

questions.stem: Look at this series: R, QQ, P, OO, N, ... What term should come next?
questions.explanation: The letters walk backward one at a time (R, Q, P, O, N, M) and every second term is doubled, so the next term is MM. M forgets the doubling, MMM triples it and LL skips a letter.

questions.stem: Look at this series: K, L, K, LL, K, LLL, K, ... What term should come next?
questions.explanation: A single K sits between groups of L that grow by one letter each time, so after LLL and K comes LLLL. LLL repeats the previous group, K continues the wrong strand and KKKK grows the letter that never changes.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 5J, K9, 5L, M9, ... What term should come next?
questions.explanation: The letters run J, K, L, M, N in order and the numbers alternate 5 and 9, with the 5 terms putting the number first. So the next term is 5N. N5 has the right characters in the wrong order, 5M repeats the letter and 9N pairs the correct letter with the wrong number.

questions.stem: Look at this series: C3, F12, I48, ... What term should come next?
questions.explanation: The letter advances three each time (C, F, I, L) and the number is multiplied by four each time (3, 12, 48, 192). L96 doubles instead of quadrupling, L144 triples and K192 advances the letter only two.

questions.stem: Look at this series: B5, D9, F13, H17, ... What term should come next?
questions.explanation: The letter moves ahead two and the number climbs by four, so H17 is followed by J21. J19 adds two to the number, J25 adds eight and I21 moves the letter only one.

questions.stem: Look at this series: AE, DH, GK, ___, MQ. What term is missing?
questions.explanation: Both letters advance three at a time, so A, D, G, J, M and E, H, K, N, Q give JN. JM moves the second letter only two, IN moves the first letter only two and NJ is the answer reversed.

questions.stem: Look at this series: ___, EI, IM, MQ, QU. What term should come first?
questions.explanation: Each letter jumps ahead four, so stepping back four from E and I gives AE. AI leaves the second letter alone, BF steps back only three and EA is the answer written backward.

questions.stem: Look at this series: MCF, MEF, MGF, ___, MKF. What term is missing?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters never change and the middle letter advances two, so C, E, G, I, K gives MIF. MJF pushes the middle letter one too far, MIG moves the last letter as well and FIM is the answer reversed.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(3^3\)   B. \(2^4\)   C. \(9\times 3\)
questions.explanation: A is 27 and C is 27, while B is 16, so A and C tie and B is smaller. Reading \(3^3\) as \(3\times 3=9\) or \(2^4\) as 32 produces the other orderings.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. 25% of 80   B. \(\frac{1}{5}\) of 100   C. \(0.2\times 90\)
questions.explanation: A and B are both 20 and C is 18. Twenty percent and one-fifth are the same fraction, so the tie is between A and B, not with C.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(0.5\times 10^3\)   B. \(50\times 10^1\)   C. \(5\times 10^2\)
questions.explanation: All three equal 500. Moving the decimal point three places in A gives 5000 and moving it two places gives 50, which are the two most common slips here.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(8+4\times 3\)   B. \((8+4)\times 3\)   C. \(8\times 3+4\)
questions.explanation: A is 20, B is 36 and C is 28, so A < C < B. Working A from left to right gives 36 and makes A look equal to B.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(\frac{3}{4}\) of 48   B. \(\frac{2}{3}\) of 54   C. \(\frac{5}{6}\) of 42
questions.explanation: A and B are both 36 and C is 35. Dividing by the numerator instead of the denominator turns A into 64 and B into 81.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(\sqrt{169}\)   B. \(6^2-23\)   C. \(3^3-13\)
questions.explanation: A is 13, B is 36 - 23 = 13 and C is 27 - 13 = 14, so A and B tie and C is one larger. Treating an exponent as a multiplier makes B negative or C negative.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. 150% of 20   B. 20% of 150   C. 2.5% of 1200
questions.explanation: Each one is 30. Percent is commutative, so A and B must match and 2.5% of 1200 is 30 rather than 300.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(25\times 8\)   B. \(15\times 14\)   C. \(40\times 5\)
questions.explanation: A and C are both 200 and B is 210. Computing 15 x 14 as 150 + 50 gives 200 and makes all three look equal.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(2^3\times 2^2\)   B. \(2^6\)   C. \(4^3\)
questions.explanation: A is 32 because the exponents add to give \(2^5\), while B and C are both 64. Multiplying the exponents instead of adding them makes A look equal to B and C.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. 30% of 90   B. \(\frac{3}{8}\) of 64   C. 40% of 55
questions.explanation: A is 27, B is 24 and C is 22, so C < B < A. Dividing 64 by eight carelessly gives 21 for B and reverses the bottom two.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(20-(6-2)\)   B. \((20-6)-2\)   C. \(20-6-2\)
questions.explanation: A is 16 while B and C are both 12. Subtraction groups from the left, so removing the parentheses in A changes its value but removing them in B does not.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(250\div 10^2\)   B. \(0.25\times 10^2\)   C. \(2.5\times 10^2\)
questions.explanation: A is 2.5, B is 25 and C is 250, each ten times the one before. Every distractor comes from moving a decimal point the wrong number of places.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(\frac{2}{5}\) of 80   B. 55% of 40   C. \(\frac{1}{3}\) of 96
questions.explanation: A and C are both 32 and B is 22. Using one-fifth instead of two-fifths gives 16 for A, which drops it below B.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(2^6\)   B. \(6^2\)   C. \(3^4\)
questions.explanation: A is 64, B is 36 and C is 81. Swapping the base and the exponent in A gives 36 and makes A look equal to B.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(48\div 4+2\)   B. \(48\div (4+2)\)   C. \(48\div 4-2\)
questions.explanation: A is 14, B is 8 and C is 10, so B < C < A. Applying the parentheses to A instead of B swaps the two largest values.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. 60% of 45   B. 45% of 60   C. 15% of 200
questions.explanation: A and B are both 27 because the two factors simply trade places and C is 30.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(5^2-\sqrt{81}\)   B. \(\sqrt{81}+5\)   C. \(3^2+8\)
questions.explanation: A is 25 - 9 = 16, B is 9 + 5 = 14 and C is 9 + 8 = 17. Reading \(5^2\) as 10 collapses A to 1 and reading \(3^2\) as 6 ties C to B.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(2^2\times 5^2\)   B. \(10^2\)   C. \(2\times 5^2\)
questions.explanation: A is 4 x 25 = 100 and B is 100, while C is 2 x 25 = 50 because only the five is squared. Squaring the product in C would wrongly make it 100 as well.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(9\times 11\)   B. \(10^2-1\)   C. \(48+50\)
questions.explanation: A and B are both 99 and C is 98. A single careless addition in C is what makes the all-equal option tempting.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(\frac{3}{5}\) of 55   B. \(\frac{5}{8}\) of 56   C. \(\frac{2}{7}\) of 112
questions.explanation: A is 33, B is 35 and C is 32. Each distractor comes from using the unit fraction instead of the given one in exactly one of the three.

questions.stem: What number is 9 less than the square of 8?
questions.explanation: The square of 8 is 64 and 64 - 9 = 55. Adding gives 73, doubling instead of squaring gives 7 and subtracting nine twice gives 46.

questions.stem: Three-fifths of what number is 27?
questions.explanation: Divide by three and multiply by five: 27 / 3 = 9 and 9 x 5 = 45. Taking three-fifths of 27 gives 16.2 and stopping after one of the two steps gives 135 or 9.

questions.stem: Twice the amount by which 15 exceeds a certain number is 18. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Half of 18 is 9, so 15 exceeds the number by 9 and the number is 15 - 9 = 6. Nine is the gap itself rather than the number, 24 comes from adding the 9 to 15, and 12 comes from doubling only the 15 and then subtracting.

questions.stem: One-half of what number is six more than one-third of that number?
questions.explanation: One-half minus one-third is one-sixth, so one-sixth of the number is six and the number is 36. Subtracting the fractions as one-third gives 18 and as one-twelfth gives 72.

questions.stem: What number is 4 more than the cube of 5?
questions.explanation: The cube of 5 is 125 and 125 + 4 = 129. Subtracting gives 121, tripling instead of cubing gives 19 and 125 is the cube alone.

questions.stem: The sum of 12 and what number, when doubled, equals 46?
questions.explanation: Half of 46 is 23, so the sum is 23 and the number is 23 - 12 = 11. Twenty-three is the sum rather than the number and 34 comes from never halving.

questions.stem: Four times a number is the same as that number increased by 27. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Four of the number minus one of the number leaves three of them, so 27 / 3 = 9. Dividing 27 by four gives 6.75 and 36 is four times the answer.

questions.stem: Three times the sum of 8 and what number equals seven times that number?
questions.explanation: Distributing gives 24 + 3 of the number = 7 of the number, so four of them equal 24 and the number is six. Forgetting to distribute the three gives four and 14 is the sum rather than the number.

questions.stem: What number is 30 more than 40% of 150?
questions.explanation: Forty percent of 150 is 60 and 60 + 30 = 90. Adding first and then taking the percent gives 76 and subtracting instead of adding gives 30.

questions.stem: What number is 8 more than three-eighths of 96?
questions.explanation: Three-eighths of 96 is 36 and 36 + 8 = 44. Subtracting gives 28, adding before taking the fraction gives 39 and 36 skips the second step.

questions.stem: Sixty percent of what number is 8 more than 40 percent of that number?
questions.explanation: The gap between 60% and 40% is 20% of the number, so 20% of it is eight and the number is 40. Dividing eight by 0.4 gives 20 and by 0.1 gives 80.

questions.stem: The product of 6 and what number is 12 less than 90?
questions.explanation: Ninety minus 12 is 78 and 78 / 6 = 13. Adding the 12 gives 17, 78 is the product itself and 15 ignores the 12 altogether.

questions.stem: What number, when increased by one-fourth of itself, equals 45?
questions.explanation: The number plus a quarter of it is five-fourths of it, so the number is 45 x 4 / 5 = 36. Subtracting a quarter of 45 gives 33.75 and using three-fourths gives 60.

questions.stem: What number is 7 less than twice 19?
questions.explanation: Twice 19 is 38 and 38 - 7 = 31. Adding gives 45, subtracting before doubling gives 24 and 12 forgets to double.

questions.stem: Two-fifths of what number is 18 less than that number?
questions.explanation: The number minus two-fifths of it leaves three-fifths, so three-fifths of it is 18 and the number is 30. Forty-five comes from multiplying 18 by five-halves and 12 is two-fifths of the answer.

questions.stem: Two-thirds of the product of 9 and 6 is what number?
questions.explanation: The product is 54 and two-thirds of 54 is 36. Eighteen is one-third of it, 81 uses the reciprocal three-halves and 54 is the product alone.

questions.stem: Fifteen percent of what number is 12?
questions.explanation: Divide: 12 / 0.15 = 80. Taking 15% of 12 gives 1.8, multiplying gives 180 and misplacing the decimal in the division gives eight.

questions.stem: The sum of a number and its double is 51. What is the number?
questions.explanation: A number plus twice itself is three of them, so 51 / 3 = 17. Dividing by two gives 25.5, 34 is the double and dividing by four gives 12.75.

questions.stem: What number, when squared, gives a result 24 greater than 25?
questions.explanation: The square is 25 + 24 = 49, so the number is seven. Forty-nine is the square rather than the number and subtracting instead of adding leaves one.

questions.stem: Four less than one-third of what number is 10?
questions.explanation: One-third of the number is 10 + 4 = 14, so the number is 42. Subtracting the four instead gives 18 and 14 is one-third of the answer.

questions.stem: What number is 25 percent of 60 percent of 200?
questions.explanation: Sixty percent of 200 is 120 and a quarter of 120 is 30. Adding the two percents gives 170 and 120 stops after the first step.

questions.stem: When a number is divided by 4 and then increased by 6, the result is 21. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Undo in reverse order: 21 - 6 = 15 and 15 x 4 = 60. Adding the six instead gives 108 and multiplying before subtracting gives 78.

questions.stem: Twice a number, decreased by 5, is the same as the number increased by 7. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Two of the number minus one of them leaves one and 7 + 5 = 12. Nineteen is the value each side reaches and 24 is twice the answer.

questions.stem: One-third of what number is the same as 40 percent of 45?
questions.explanation: Forty percent of 45 is 18, so one-third of the number is 18 and the number is 54. Eighteen and six are intermediate values and 135 ignores the percent.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 1, 3, 4, 7, 11, 18, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two before it, so 11 + 18 = 29. You get 25 by adding the wrong pair, 7 + 18, and skipping a term, 36 by doubling the last term instead of adding the pair and 47 by running the rule one step too far, 18 + 29.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 3, 6, 18, 72, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: The multiplier itself grows: two, then three, then four, so the next step is times five and 72 x 5 = 360. You get 288 by repeating the multiplier of four, 216 by dropping back to three and 1800 by taking one step too many.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 5, 7, 11, ___, 35, 67. What number is missing?
questions.explanation: The gaps double rather than grow by a fixed amount: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, so the missing term is 11 + 8 = 19, which checks against 35 - 16. You get 15 by repeating the gap of four, 23 by assuming the gaps climb by two and 27 by counting back eight from 35 instead of 16.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 4, 8, 11, 22, 25, 50, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: Two operations take turns, doubling and then adding three, and after a doubling it is the turn of the addition, so 50 + 3 = 53. You get 100 by doubling when it is the addition's turn, 106 by carrying out both halves of the rule at once and 47 by subtracting the three instead of adding it.

questions.stem: Look at this series: ___, 25, 36, 49, 64. What number should come first?
questions.explanation: These are the squares of 5, 6, 7 and 8, so the term before 25 is the square of 4, which is 16. You get 4 by giving the number that is squared rather than the square itself, 15 by assuming a gap of ten and 14 by stepping back 11, which is the gap that comes after this one rather than the one before it.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 3, 40, 6, 40, 12, 40, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: Two series take turns and one of them never moves: 3, 6, 12 doubles while every other term stays at 40, and the doubling series takes the next turn, so the answer is 24. You get 40 by continuing the standing series when it is not its turn, 18 by reading the moving series as adding six and 48 by doubling twice.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 512, 384, 288, 216, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: Each term is three-fourths of the one before it: 512 becomes 384, 384 becomes 288 and 288 becomes 216, so the next term is three-fourths of 216, which is 162. You get 144 by subtracting 72 again, the gap you just used, as though the series fell by a fixed amount each time. You get 180 by shrinking that gap by half, from 72 to 36, instead of taking three-fourths of it. You get 108 by taking the ratio to be one half rather than three-fourths.

questions.stem: Look at this series: ___, \(\frac{3}{7}\), \(\frac{4}{9}\), \(\frac{5}{11}\), \(\frac{6}{13}\). What term should come first?
questions.explanation: The numerator climbs by one and the denominator by two, so stepping back from \(\frac{3}{7}\) gives \(\frac{2}{5}\). You get \(\frac{1}{5}\) by taking two off the numerator as well as the denominator, \(\frac{2}{6}\) by taking only one off the denominator and \(\frac{4}{9}\) by running the series forward instead of backward.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 2, 30, 3, 4, 27, 9, 6, 24, 27, 8, 21, ___. What number should come next?
questions.explanation: Three sequences take turns. The first, third, fifth terms and so on run 2, 4, 6, 8, going up by two. The second, fifth, eighth and eleventh run 30, 27, 24, 21, going down by three. The third strand is 3, 9, 27, so it triples and the next term is 81. The choice 63 continues the down-by-three strand, 10 continues the up-by-two strand, and 54 doubles 27 rather than tripling it.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(\frac{5}{8}\)   B. \(\frac{10}{16}\)   C. \(\frac{3}{5}\)
questions.explanation: \(\frac{10}{16}\) reduces to \(\frac{5}{8}\), so A and B are the same 0.625, while C is 0.6. Reasoning that fifths are bigger pieces than eighths puts C on top, comparing the numerators and denominators separately makes B look bigger than A and calling all three "a little over a half" ties them.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(\sqrt{36}+\sqrt{64}\)   B. \(\sqrt{100}\)   C. \(\sqrt{36+64}\)
questions.explanation: A is 6 + 8 = 14, while C is \(\sqrt{100}\) and so is B, both 10. Splitting the root across the sum in C gives 14 and ties it to A. Halving 100 instead of rooting it makes B 50 and the largest, while combining A's two roots into a single root of 100 makes all three read 10.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(\frac{3}{4}\div\frac{1}{2}\)   B. \(\frac{3}{4}\times 2\)   C. \(\frac{3}{4}\div 2\)
questions.explanation: Dividing by \(\frac{1}{2}\) is the same as multiplying by two, so A and B are both \(\frac{3}{2}\), while C is \(\frac{3}{8}\). Reading A as a division by two ties it to C, turning the first fraction upside down instead of the second gives \(\frac{2}{3}\) for A and dividing the wrong way round in C gives \(2\div\frac{3}{4}\), which is larger than B.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(-8+5\)   B. \(8-5\)   C. \(-8-5\)
questions.explanation: A is -3, B is 3 and C is -13, so B is largest and C smallest. Ignoring the leading minus sign in A ties it to B, judging -13 as larger than -3 because 13 is larger than 3 puts C on top and reading A as 8 + 5 makes it 13 and the largest.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. the number of factors of 12   B. the number of factors of 16   C. the number of factors of 18
questions.explanation: Twelve has 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12 and 18 has 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 and 18, six each, while 16 has only 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16. Counting factor pairs instead of factors gives three for each and ties them, since 16 pairs 4 with itself; assuming the larger number must have more factors lifts B; and forgetting that 9 divides 18 drops C to five.

questions.stem: Examine A, B and C. Choose the best answer.  A. \(0.3^2\)   B. \(0.3\times 3\)   C. \(\sqrt{0.09}\)
questions.explanation: A is 0.09, C is the number that squares to 0.09 and so is 0.3, and B is 0.9. Losing a decimal place in A makes it 0.9 and ties it to B, taking C as 0.03 by copying both decimal places drops it below A and rooting the 9 while ignoring the decimal point makes C 3 and the largest.

questions.stem: What number is five more than the square root of 144?
questions.explanation: The square root of 144 is 12 and 12 + 5 = 17. You get 7 by subtracting the five instead of adding it, 72 by halving 144 rather than taking its root and 149 by adding five to 144 itself.

questions.stem: The sum of three consecutive whole numbers is 42. What is the smallest of the three?
questions.explanation: The three numbers are 13, 14 and 15, and the smallest is 13. Fourteen is the middle number, which is what dividing 42 by three gives on its own, 15 is the largest of the three and 12 comes from stepping two below that middle number instead of one.

questions.stem: The average of 14 and what number is 20?
questions.explanation: The two numbers must total 2 x 20 = 40, so the missing one is 40 - 14 = 26. Six comes from subtracting 14 from the average itself, 34 from adding 20 to 14 and 40 is the total of the pair rather than the missing number.

questions.stem: Sixty divided by a certain number gives four more than eight. What is that number?
questions.explanation: Four more than eight is 12, so 60 divided by the number is 12 and the number is 60 / 12 = 5. Twelve is the result of the division rather than the number you divide by, 720 comes from multiplying 60 by 12 and 15 comes from dividing by four less than eight.

questions.stem: A number divided by 7 leaves a quotient of 8 and a remainder of 3. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Multiply the divisor by the quotient and put the remainder back: 7 x 8 + 3 = 59. Fifty-six leaves the remainder out, 53 subtracts it instead of adding it and 11 comes from adding the quotient and the remainder rather than multiplying first.

questions.explanation: Every other letter of the alphabet is written out and then cut into groups of three, so after M, O and Q come S, U and W. RTV starts the group one letter early, SUV moves the last letter only one place and SUY moves it four instead of two.

questions.stem: The number that is 5 less than 40 is how many times the number that is 3 more than 4?
questions.explanation: Untangle the sentence one piece at a time. Five less than 40 is 35, and 3 more than 4 is 7. The question asks how many times 7 goes into 35, so divide: \(35\div7=5\). Choosing 7 answers with the second number itself rather than the comparison. Choosing 28 subtracts, \(35-7\), instead of dividing. Choosing 245 multiplies the two numbers.

questions.stem: Look at this series: 40, 38, 35, 31, ___, 20. What number is missing?
questions.explanation: The amount taken away grows by one each step: \(40-2=38\), \(38-3=35\) and \(35-4=31\), so the next step is 5 and the missing term is \(31-5=26\). The 20 at the end confirms it, since \(26-6=20\). Choosing 27 repeats the previous step of 4 instead of letting it grow. Choosing 23 doubles the step from 4 to 8 rather than raising it by one. Choosing 25 works backward from 20 with a step of 5, when the step on that side of the blank is 6.

Even taking \(\pi\) as 3 the curve is 12 cm and A comes to 20 cm, still the shortest. Counting A as a whole circle gives about 25.1 cm and lifts it above B. Comparing the space inside instead of the distance around gives about 25, 36 and 36, which ties B to C. Using the 8 cm straight edge as the radius gives about 33 cm and makes A the longest.

Assuming a four-sided figure always has four right angles makes all three equal at 90 degrees. Picking out the largest angle drawn in each figure, 115 then 100 then 120, ranks them B, A, C.
